<!-- Generated by `node scripts/docs-reference.mjs`. Do not edit. -->

A clip recorded at 44.1 kHz will still play correctly in a 48 kHz project — Soundscaper converts on the fly — but for a delivery that must be at one rate, or before an effect that expects it, you can convert the clip itself. Resampling recalculates every sample at the new rate and keeps the timing exactly.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **Tracks → Resample**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Open the clip's menu from the **Clip menu** button on its name bar and choose **Clip properties**. Press **Resample**, set the rate to `44100` and press **Resample** again. The clip’s properties show its current rate; 44100 Hz is CD standard.
4. Press **Play** to listen, then **Stop**.
   *You should see:* The clip sounds exactly as before; only its stored rate has changed.

## Tips

- Resampling is an edit and can be undone.
- Going down in rate discards the highest frequencies; going up adds nothing but is harmless.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
